title: Flying Cows and Smart Drones: How Phone Companies Get Ready for Hurricanes
summary:
Have you ever lost cell service during a big storm? It’s scary, right? Well, phone companies are fighting back with some seriously cool tools — including flying “COWs” and AI-powered drones.

Hurricane season runs from June to November. Even though experts predict fewer storms this year, just one powerful hurricane can knock out cell towers for days. That’s why companies like Verizon and AT&T start planning a whole week before a storm hits.

Verizon uses drones to snap “before” and “after” pictures of an area. Then, artificial intelligence (AI) — that’s computer brainpower — compares them to find exactly where towers are damaged. This helps repair crews fix things super fast, sometimes in minutes instead of hours.

They also have a fleet of backup gadgets with funny animal names. A COW is a “cell on wheels” — basically a cell tower on a truck. A HAWK is a drone that can fly a small tower into the sky to beam signals down to people below. How cool is that?

AT&T doesn’t mess around either. They have boats, barges, and even helicopters to reach flooded or blocked areas. They’ve also merged their disaster teams so they can respond to hurricanes, wildfires, and snowstorms all year round.

If the power goes out, some carriers can switch your phone to free satellite service. AI also helps stretch battery life on backup towers so they last longer. As one expert said, people might be patient without electricity, but they really want their smartphones to work.

And before anyone else gets connected, first responders like firefighters and paramedics get priority. They need reliable service to send medical data and live updates from ambulances. So next time a storm is coming, remember: behind the scenes, high-tech helpers are already on the move.
why_it_matters: Knowing that companies have backup plans can be reassuring — when a hurricane hits, reliable phone service helps you stay in touch with family and gets help faster.

background_read: After Hurricane Katrina struck in 2005, many cell towers were destroyed and millions couldn’t call for help for days.
Verizon and AT&T (two of the largest U.S. cellphone providers) now prepare a week ahead of any major storm, using flying drones and portable towers.
Today, artificial intelligence helps crews find damage faster, but backup tools like COWs and HAWKs are still needed when infrastructure is wiped out.
Article_Structure: WHO: Phone companies like Verizon and AT&T, and first responders such as firefighters and paramedics.
WHAT: They use flying drones with AI, mobile cell towers called COWs, and HAWK drones to quickly repair cell service after hurricanes.
WHERE: Across hurricane-prone regions of the United States during hurricane season (June to November).
WHY: So people can call for help, and emergency workers can send medical data and updates without interruption.

perspectives.description: Emergency officials praise drones and AI because they help repair crews fix outages in minutes instead of hours, saving lives.
Some worry that not all communities get these high-tech tools, so rural or poor areas might still lose service for days.
Cell towers have always been vulnerable to storms; every year, phone companies improve their equipment, but no system is perfect.
